title: ASML says it sold 'absolutely nothing' in Europe in 2026
titleZh: ASML says it sold 'absolutely nothing' in Europe in 2026
author: MC995
relevanceReason: 命中 1 个 AI/科技关键词。
summaryRaw: As the world's only supplier of EUV lithography systems, ASML is Europe's largest company by market capitalization, currently valued at around $660 billion. But it earned almost nothing in Europe this year, down from 1% of total profits in 2025 and 5% in 2024. Why? European chipmakers bought no lithography equipment from ASML in 2026 — and the company is calling on EU authorities to help create demand for European chips.Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.

children.author: uecker
children.textRawHtml:
If you want to measure all economic activity than one has to include also illegal activity. Whether any activity - legal or not - has any "value" in a non-economic sense is a different question. GDP can certainly be criticized. But it seems you point was mainly that industrial production went to down in Europa since 2007, but I can also not see this.

The main issues Europa has are dependency on Energy imports, an unhealthy but fixable dependency on US IT tech, an ongoing war with Russia, and an aging population. Renewables are are really good idea, immigration would also help a lot, but is politically difficult.

children.author: api
children.textRawHtml:
What's special about fossil fuel? Is a kilowatt-hour from burning carbon magically able to power an economy better than one from a solar panel, a wind turbine, or a nuclear reactor?

I think you could make that argument (at least structurally) as late as the 2000s when batteries and solar were still un-economical. Today it's very possible to power a modern economy without fossil fuels in almost every sector except long haul trucking, a few industrial processes, and aviation, and those together are a small percentage of overall fossil fuel use. Aviation and trucking are less than 10% of oil use.

Europe doesn't have an energy shortage that's not self-inflicted. Becoming dependent on Russian gas combined with anti-nuclear in Germany probably contribute. German greens are basically an advertising arm of Gazprom. (Just like how America's huge inflation is self-inflicted via dumb tariffs and unnecessary wars. We should pay politicians an extra bonus to do nothing.)

The most likely explanation for Europe's stagnation is a mix of stifling bureaucracy, low birth rates, brain drain (mostly to the US), and policies that are explicitly growth-limiting.

children.author: toasty228
children.textRawHtml:
> What's special about fossil fuel?

Is this a real question?

- just bend down to harvest, nature has done all the work over millions of years

- energy dense as fuck

- reliable, it doesn't matter if you have sun, wind, if it's winter or summer

- easy to store and transport

- can be transformed into fertiliser, which allowed us to feed more people, for cheaper and more easily

- literal building block of everything that made what the world is today: plastics, medicine, synthetic fibers, etc.

- allowed us to transform materials which required high temperatures: metal, glas, etc.

We're quite literally a fossil fuel society...

All that is historically true, but most new energy being added to the grid is now renewable. Solar and batteries continue to get cheaper and it's already the cheapest source of new power in sunny places.

I have seen this raised as yet another interesting Fermi paradox idea: maybe our planet is unusual in that it stored up a giant store of easily exploitable energy to bootstrap a technological civilization.
